result.title: Rethinking Offline On-Policy Distillation: From Scalar Advantages to Distributional Supervision
result.summary: On-policy distillation (OPD) transfers teacher capabilities through token-level feedback on student-generated trajectories, but repeatedly evaluating fresh rollouts with the teacher is computationally expensive. Offline methods such as Lightning OPD reduce this cost by caching recorded tokens' teacher log-probabilities on fixed reference rollouts. By extending the idea to a multi-turn agentic search setup, we find that it consistently underperforms the SFT starting point trained by the same teacher. We empirically observe greater teacher--reference mismatch than in mathematical reasoning and post-training distributional flattening, and theoretically show that scalar advantage supervision on fixed rollouts admits solutions with flattened output distributions under suitable conditions. Motivated by these findings, we propose Distributional On-Policy Distillation (DistOPD), a simple yet effective offline OPD method that retains candidate-token probabilities from both reference and teacher at selected positions and aggregates the remaining parts into a residual token. On agentic search, DistOPD achieves performance comparable to online OPD while improving student--teacher alignment and using training GPU-hours comparable to Lightning OPD.

AI.brief_summary: 该文分析离线 on-policy 蒸馏在 multi-turn agentic search 上劣于同教师 SFT 的现象，指出教师与参考轨迹不匹配及分布扁平化问题，并提出保存候选 token 概率、其余合并为残差 token 的 DistOPD 分布级监督方法。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「标量优势监督导致输出分布扁平化」的诊断与分布级残差监督，可能为 LVR 轨迹训练中的监督信号设计与信息坍缩核查提供线索，但该文未涉及视觉 latent 状态，需进一步核查可迁移性。
